thread:
Anika: Quick FYI — after the AMS region change some EU customers report higher p95 for short-chat requests. Thinking of switching routing logic from static region-priority to a per-request latency probe + tier-aware fallback. Pros/cons?
Sam: Hmm. probe per-request sounds heavy. Do you mean a lightweight TCP/HTTP ping before routing?
Anika: Exactly, a small RTT probe (50–100ms timebox) against candidate endpoints and pick the lowest latency one that meets capacity. Keep in mind customer tier must still prefer reserved capacity pools.
Tomas: We should consider caching probe results for short windows — say 5s — and smoothing to avoid flip-flopping on noisy pings. Also, probes don't reflect cold KV or Model-variant warmup.
Maya: Also model variant compatibility. If we route to eu-west-1 but the requested model variant (quantized v2) isn't available there, fallback should consider variant compatibility before pure latency.
Anika: Right — proposed ordered decision tree: 1) Filter endpoints by tier/entitlement (reserved/dedicated) 2) Filter by model-variant compatibility 3) Probe latency and select lowest within threshold 4) If no candidate, escalate to region fallback policy.
Sam: That ordering makes sense. A couple notes: probes must be non-blocking for high-throughput bursts. Could we piggyback probes on real requests when capacity allows?
Tomas: For burst workloads piggybacking helps but adds variability. I'd prefer async health stream that continuously measures inter-region RTT per dataplane node and aggregates at control plane. Then per-req, consult the recent bucket (eg 2–5s window).
Maya: For model variants, we need to encode compatibility in the model catalog (fields: variant_id, region_available, cold_warm_score). Then routing can prefer regions with warm cache for that variant.
Kevin: How about console UX? Operators should be able to: toggle latency-probing, set smoothing window, and define a per-tenant override (force-region). Keep canary flags for rollout.
Anika: Yes — add a "Routing Debug" view showing chosen endpoint, probe latencies, and why others were filtered (entitlement/compatibility/capacity). Important for SRE debugging.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout-started anika/routing-probe-feature v1 -> canary (5% traffic)
Sam: For quotas: if we route to a reserved pool, quota enforcement must happen before routing decision (so we don't send requests that will be rejected). That implies checking per-tenant tokens/allocations synchronously. Cheap cache for tokens will help.
Tomas: Edge case — partial-model-match: backend can serve a high-precision variant but not the requested quantized one. Do we allow fallback to a compatible but costlier variant? That should be policy-driven per-tenant.
Maya: Add a per-tenant policy: allow_variant_escalation = [never, auto-with-consent, always]. Default = auto-with-consent for enterprise. If auto, annotate response with a header and billing might differ.
Anika: Good. Also circuit breaker: if probe shows region latency degradation or x% 5xxs, mark region as degraded and exclude for a cooldown. We already have circuit logic but wire it into routing weight decisions.
Sam: Implementation plan suggestion: - control plane: maintain endpoint inventory + recent health/time-series - policy engine: implement filter chain (tier -> variant -> capacity -> probe/score) - dataplane: expose a lightweight probe endpoint and per-req metadata header for debugging - console: feature flags + debug UI + per-tenant override panel
Tomas: Scoring idea: combine smoothed latency (L) and capacity headroom (H) into a score S = alpha * normalized(L) + (1-alpha) * normalized(1/H). Tunable alpha by tenant tier (premium -> favor latency more).
Maya: We'll need telemetry changes: emit routing_decision events with fields: chosen_endpoint, candidates, probe_samples, model_variant_used, reason_codes. That will help postmortems when customers complain.
Kevin: UX: expose a rollout control: when enabling probe-based routing, we should support phased rollout: first synthetic traffic (internal), then canary customers by tag, then % fanout. Console should show impact on p50/p95 and cost delta (cost increases if we escalate variants).
Anika: Sample policy YAML for review:
```yaml
policy_name: eu_latency_probe_tiered
entitlement: [reserved, hosted]
variant_policy:
  allow_escalation: auto-with-consent
probe:
  timeout_ms: 80
  smoothing_window_s: 5
scoring:
  alpha_by_tier:
    premium: 0.8
    standard: 0.5
fallbacks:
  - prefer_same_region_with_variant
  - prefer_other_region_reserved
  - escalate_to_global_pool
```
Sam: Love the YAML. Implementation note: set probe timeout conservatively to avoid adding tail latency. If probe timeout expires, treat endpoint as high-latency and only pick if no other options.
Tomas: Metrics to add: probe_success_rate, probe_p95_ms, routing_decision_count_by_reason, variant_escalation_count. Also histogram of per-tenant chosen-region distribution.
Maya: We should write an integration test that simulates region flaps and verifies we don't oscillate (use fake probe stream, assert smoothing).
Anika: OK I'll draft an RFC with the above and include config examples + telemetry schema. Can we get reviews from eng-runtime and infra?
Sam: I'll review. Happy to help with dataplane probe endpoint.
Tomas: I'll own the policy engine bits.
Maya: I'll add model-catalog compatibility fields and tests.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout-complete anika/routing-probe-feature v1 -> canary
Kevin: Thanks all — when RFC ready ping #eng-platform for formal review. :thumbsup:
Maya: One more thing — add a dry-run mode where routing decisions are logged but not applied. Helps measure real impact before flip.
Anika: Great call. Dry-run + telemetry first then phased rollout.
